adjudication_rationale: The torch.empty padding could feed stale indices into CUDA-graph attention and cause out-of-bounds access; the root cause is not shown to be hardware-only. Sides with coder A.

The AMD prefix-prefill path overflowed offset arithmetic into negative addresses; large-offset edge tests on ROCm are the cheapest plausible detector, with memcheck also useful. Sides with neither coder.
The stale CUDA-graph track-buffer tail corrupts cache-hit rescoring only across decode, cache insertion, and replay, so full serving/cache coverage is primary. Sides with coder A.
The PR ties a nightly GSM8K accuracy failure to FlashInfer KV-cache quantization, but gives little hardware detail. Sides with coder A.
The sliding-window FA3 path failed correctness tests on H100; Hopper/FA3 CI with those tests would likely have caught it. Sides with coder B.
The KT wrapper silently missed the final-layer no-deferral rule after an API refactor; this is configuration/backend integration rather than hardware-specific behavior. Sides with neither coder.
The record only says to fix an AMD RoPE definition and check AMD CI, without enough failure evidence to confirm production kernel correctness. Sides with coder B.
The JIT RMSNorm kernel lacked small/oversized hidden-size handling; the evidence points to a size-coverage edge rather than a B200-only problem. Sides with neither coder.
The FlashInfer CUTLASS MoE FP4 path caused model accuracy loss under specific quantized workload settings, not an identified hardware-only failure. Sides with neither coder.
The SM90 CUTLASS FP8 GEMM had mismatched load predicates and values causing illegal memory access; sanitizer on failing shapes is the direct detector. Sides with coder A.
Dropping fixed_split_size made FlashInfer SWA/cross-attention outputs vary with batch composition despite deterministic inference. Sides with coder B.
The PR is primarily performance work and only mentions an int64 offset issue without a concrete failure symptom or before/after correctness evidence. Sides with coder B.
The ROCm Quark GLM-5.2 path crashed from sparse-MLA metadata and FP8 scale-shape issues, with ROCm model coverage primary and scale-shape tests also plausible. Sides with neither coder.
The TRTLLM allreduce fusion path is reported to cause illegal memory access, but the record does not identify a specific affected GPU. Sides with coder B.
A global routed-experts capturer let speculative draft writes pollute target output state, requiring spec/MoE serving coverage. Sides with coder B.
DeepSeek V3.2 MTP in V1 mode crashed in the NSA backend during warmup, best exposed by a model startup/spec-decode test. Sides with coder B.
A binding typo caused random or empty output only on Ada with CUDA 12.4+, so the decisive missing coverage is the affected hardware/compiler matrix. Sides with neither coder.
The CPU fused-MoE path instantiated CustomOps during forward and hit an unset vLLM config; CPU-path forward/serving coverage is needed. Sides with coder A.
NemotronH MTP plus chunked prefill produced garbage outputs, which is a hybrid serving integration failure rather than hardware-specific behavior. Sides with coder A.
The linked issue reports a B200 FlashMLA sparse accuracy drop; B200 coverage is primary, with full model accuracy workload also necessary. Sides with neither coder.
The cache kernel accessed beyond block_table_stride and the added boundary test was verified under compute-sanitizer. Sides with coder A.
DeepSeek-V2.5 FP8 crashed in the CUTLASS MoE scale-shape path; scale-shape unit coverage is the cheapest plausible detector. Sides with coder A.
The ROCm AITER MXFP4 path routed preshuffled weights to the wrong codegen branch, producing nonsense outputs; ROCm coverage with the real layout is key. Sides with coder B.
DP padding made the pooled-indexer bridge reject logical rows under breakable prefill; the root is shape handling, not the tested GB300 hardware. Sides with coder B.
FlashInfer sampling API changes broke top-p/top-k sampling; a sampler configuration/reference test is cheaper than full serving, though serving would also catch it. Sides with coder B.
The EXAONE head_dim=80 case requested Triton but still hit FlashInfer, a backend-selection edge that can be tested by varying head dimensions. Sides with neither coder.
The CUTLASS MoE pre-reorder address calculation overflowed int32 for large destination rows, causing illegal or wrong writes. Sides with neither coder.
The top-k renorm kernels used int32 flattened offsets, so large batch-vocab products could corrupt memory accesses. Sides with coder B.
The fused allreduce/RMSNorm path assumed a 2-D tensor and crashed on the transformers backend; varying activation ranks is the direct edge test. Sides with neither coder.
The record says a CPU replacement for a Triton slot-mapping kernel was added and CPU CI softfail removed, but does not show a concrete failing production behavior. Sides with coder B.
